claims.text: Increasing Al from about 5 at.% to 10–15 at.% enhances local lattice distortion.
Increasing Al within the proposed moderate range suppresses excessive chemical short-range order.
Al-induced lattice distortion and modified chemical short-range order hinder defect mobility.
Al-induced lattice distortion and modified chemical short-range order hinder phase separation.
Elevated Al increases lattice strain and thereby raises the energy barrier for dislocation motion.
Elevated Al raises energy barriers for defect clustering.
Al-induced distortion produces balanced vacancy and interstitial mobilities.
Balanced vacancy and interstitial mobilities enhance recombination of irradiation-induced vacancy–interstitial pairs.
Al-induced distortion stabilizes the alloy against temperature-driven ordering or precipitation.
Impeded defect mobility and coarsening improve high-temperature strength.
Increasing Al within the moderate range improves environmental resistance.
Enhanced vacancy–interstitial recombination improves radiation tolerance.
Enhanced vacancy–interstitial recombination promotes cryogenic toughness.
The higher-Al alloy will have greater yield strength than the low-Al baseline after high-temperature exposure.
The higher-Al alloy will undergo less grain coarsening than the low-Al baseline during high-temperature exposure.
The higher-Al alloy will develop fewer irradiation-induced defects, including dislocation loops or precipitates, than the low-Al baseline.
The higher-Al alloy will maintain or improve cryogenic ductility and toughness relative to the low-Al baseline.
Al concentrations beyond the proposed 5–15 at.% range may cause ordered intermetallic phases such as B2 to form and negate favorable properties.
The low-Al baseline exhibits more pronounced defect clustering and phase instability under extreme conditions.
The initial as-cast alloy is described as single-phase while being allowed to have either disordered BCC or mixed FCC/BCC structure.

contradictions.description: The initial material is called single-phase, but mixed FCC/BCC is intrinsically a multiphase state.

The mediator broadly hinders defect mobility, whereas the mechanism invokes vacancy and interstitial mobility sufficient to enhance recombination; the hypothesis does not explain how mobility is selectively balanced rather than simply suppressed.
